$comment: The type catalogue - biotech MIME types. Each type is meaning, formats, a sniffer that recognises one from its bytes, and a specimen. Adding a type is a data change, not a code change; the runner reads this file and knows nothing about biology. Identifiers track EDAM (edamontology.org) so this stays interoperable rather than becoming a private dialect. The `example` is a fallback: when a user sets up a tool they normally supply their own data, and that is always the better fixture. The specimen exists so a fixture can be built when they have not.

Table.description: Rectangular data with a header row.
Table.$comment: Sniffing skips comment_prefix lines. Found by portlab/stamp on the first conformance run: its output opens with a '#' provenance header, which is not a type error.

Text.description: Unstructured text. The escape hatch - if an adapter uses this for everything, it has not been ported, only wrapped.

Directory.description: An opaque multi-file artefact produced as a unit. A BLAST database is the motivating case.

Alignment.description: Sequences padded to a common length. Not a Sequence: the gaps carry the homology claim, and downstream tools reject unaligned input.
Alignment.$comment: Found while wrapping MAFFT: aligned FASTA is lexically identical to plain FASTA on its first line, so a regex sniffer cannot separate Alignment from Sequence. The distinguishing property is structural - every record the same length - which is why `structure` exists.

alphabets.$comment: The alphabet rule, as DATA rather than code, so the Python runner and the TypeScript uploader read one source instead of drifting apart. Same pattern the sniffers already use. Two implementations are acceptable; two rules are not, and a shared corpus is what keeps them honest.
alphabets.$why_this_is_hard: Nucleotide letters are a SUBSET of protein letters, so every DNA sequence is also a syntactically valid protein sequence. Detection can therefore rule protein IN but can never rule DNA in with certainty - only with enough evidence. That asymmetry is why `ambiguous` is a real answer and not a failure to try harder.

protein_only_residues.$comment: These have no meaning in any nucleotide alphabet, ambiguity codes included. One of them is proof of protein, whatever the counts say. Deliberately excludes X and B, which are ambiguity codes in both.

thresholds.$comment: Below min_residues there is not enough evidence either way and the answer is ambiguous - which is the peer's case exactly: a short protein of only ACGT residues is indistinguishable from DNA and no threshold fixes that. Between the two fractions is the genuinely uncertain band. Counts are taken over the WHOLE file, not per record: thirty sequences are thirty times the evidence of one.

rna_over_dna.$comment: U outnumbering T means RNA. Both absent leaves dna, the commoner case.

alphabets.$contract: Declaration is the contract, detection is a check, disagreement is a finding. `ambiguous` must never be resolved by guessing: a file whose alphabet is ambiguous must not be offered as a match for a port that constrains alphabet, though it may be chosen deliberately with the ambiguity stated.
